title: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy
lede: At his first all-hands since returning, Jensen Huang reportedly told Nvidia staff the company does not need a succession plan, arguing one would add needless hierarchy.

points: CNBC reported the remarks, citing an unnamed person who was in the meeting.
Investors and analysts flagged succession as a key risk when Huang resigned earlier this month after admitting to extramarital affairs.
Nvidia is unusually flat: Huang says he has about 60 direct reports, and the company has only five executive officers.
The other four are CFO Colette Kress, who served 12 days as interim CEO, Ajay Puri, Debora Shoquist and Timothy Teter.
Huang has long argued a company's structure should follow from what it produces, as he told Lex Fridman in March.
